chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Condon, Town Hall, and the Onyx Club trio with Joe Sullivan
summary: Around 1942 he works with Condon and various clubs, taking Bobby Hackett's place in Joe Sullivan's trio with Billie Holiday as singer.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Is that when you first really got involved with Condon then, too?
Yes -- about this time. I was doing some of the Town Hall from him and, you know, we're in the war now and everything is going along---
Yeah - we're talking of this period now is '42 and early '43

And, of course, at different times in that same period of time, I even worked the Onyx Club and I worked also - Brun's and I - once just took off and went up to Jimmy Ryan's and played there for a week or two and I played at a place called The Keyboard Lounge across the street; these are all little jobbing things and I was with the--- at the Onyx I was with - at that time - doing this little thing, I had taken Bobby Hackett's place with The Joe Sullivan Trio -- with Hayes Alvis on the base -- and Joe Sullivan and me.
And, poor Bobby was having trouble then--- as I recall---
He was having a little problem with drinking at that point---

And, uh, and then - Pete Brown was the regular band in the club; we were the trio, and then we had Laura Watson as one singer and Lady Day the other -- talk about two good singers and we had a little floor show with a comedian and the whole thing; it was a lovely club--- now, all this is happening to me now, you see, I'm working all over hell--- in Chicago.
